title: Batmobile from Batman Returns Headed to Auction

body_markdown: When Batman came back to the big screen in 1989, director Tim Burton made some big changes to Gotham and its well-known cast of characters. Batman lost the camp. The Joker kept some of Cesar Romero’s panache as well as his color palette but was far more sinister. As for the Batmobile, it was all business. The long coupe, with its wraparound windows and batwing fins, was an invaluable crime-fighting tool as well as an integral part of the film’s marketing. Built on a stretched Chevrolet Impala chassis and powered by a small-block Chevy V-8 in real life, the new Batmobile was supposedly propelled by a jet turbine and had the afterburner to prove it. Like the Lincoln-Futura-based Batmobile from the TV show and 1966 movie, this iteration was packed with cool gadgets, including deployable armor, a grappling hook, and a map light that defended against the prying eyes of nosy reporter Vicki Vale. Julien's The film was a huge box office success, bringing in more than $400,000,000 and making it the highest-grossing superhero movie until it was dethroned by 2002’s *Spider-Man* . Jack Nicholson also netted himself a big payday by forgoing some of his usual salary in exchange for a bit of the box office dividends and merchandising. For the 1992 sequel, *Batman Returns* , the beloved 1989 version of the Batmobile got only minor alterations. The rear haunches were reshaped and narrowed a bit, which improved the stance and apparently solved some of the issues that arose when transporting such a wide vehicle. It also got a new paint job, glossy black in place of the matte finish it had worn previously. Soon, a screen-used Batmobile from *Batman Returns* will be up for bid at[Julien’s November 23 sale in Los Angeles](https://www.juliensauctions.com/en/auctions/the-ultimate-batmobile-auction) . The auction will also feature on-screen props and costumes as well as collectibles and production materials. If you can’t be on site to catch the auction in person, you can bid online instead. Julien's So how will this nearly 20-foot-long crime-fighting chariot stack up against some of the other Batmobiles that have previously been sold? “There isn’t as much of a following—or at least not as many people building replicas—as with the Adam West George Barris Batmobiles,” said John Wiley, Hagerty’s Director of Valuation Analytics. “Those tend to sell for about $150K. Although the original TV show car sold for[$4.6M in 2013](https://www.hagerty.com/media/video/batmobile-brings-big-bucks/) .” Wiley pointed us toward the sale of a licensed exhibition/stunt car version of the Tim-Burton-era Batmobile that[Mecum sold for $352,000](https://www.mecum.com/lots/1144589/1989-batmobile/) . While that high-quality, licensed replica of the Burton-era Batmobile brought about double its Lincoln-Futura-based predecessor, there’s no telling how much this real-deal, movie-feature Batmobile might fetch. It would take up a lot of room in a collection, and there’s absolutely no way to drive it without making a huge scene (although that may be a selling point for potential bidders). On the other hand, it did play a big role in keeping Gotham safe from the Joker, the Penguin, and Catwoman, and it’s hard to put a price tag on that kind of thing.
